description: Better Camera (code: modern_camera; core/gameplay/modern_camera/modern_camera.py): how the C-stick turns the camera while the START menu's Better Camera is enabled; Mod Settings' Max Speed multiplies every top speed here and Acceleration shortens every time constant. Lengths are the stick's, 0 at rest and 1 pushed all the way; speeds are degrees a second; times are seconds.

dead_zone.description: The stick's length under which it does nothing. The game's own pad already reads less than 30 of 127 (0.236) as nothing, so a smaller value acts as that.

full_tilt.description: The length that counts as pushed all the way: the top speed is reached here, before the stick's edge.

expo.description: The camera's response curve, 0 to 1: the turn's speed is (1 - expo) t + expo t^3 of the tilt t past the dead zone, so a small push turns slowly and precisely.

yaw_degrees_per_second.description: The top speed of the turn around the hunter (at Max Speed x1; the game's own C-stick and D-pad reach 168.75).

pitch_degrees_per_second.description: The top speed of the turn up and down (at Max Speed x1; the game's own reach 63.3).

speed_up_seconds.description: The time constant of the camera's turn speeding up toward the stick's speed (an exponential: about 63 % of the way after this long).

slow_down_seconds.description: The time constant of the camera's turn slowing down, stopping or turning the other way.

stop_degrees_per_second.description: With the stick released, a turn slower than this stops at once.

longest_frame_seconds.description: A frame longer than this (a hitch) counts as this long, so the camera never jumps.

direct.description: The quest camera's view turns by the stick in the same frame. Off, the game eases its view toward the turned angles as it does for the D-pad, which adds a second, slower smoothing.

aim_degrees_per_second.description: The aims' top speeds at full tilt, at Max Speed x1 (a bowgun over the shoulder and through the scope, the Bow), with the game's Aim Speed at its middle value and the scope at its widest view; the game's other Aim Speeds and the scope's zoom scale them as they scale the game's steps. The pitch is in degrees up (the bowguns aim 45 degrees up and 30 down, the Bow 60 both ways, in the same steps). The game's own steps at full speed: over the shoulder 66 and 40, the scope 84 and 81, the Bow 51 and 72; these are a little faster so the curve's middle does not feel slower than the game's.

aim_response.description: Each aim's response curve (as expo) and time constants (as speed_up_seconds and slow_down_seconds). Through the scope the view is the aim itself, with no camera easing it, and at full tilt the stick reaches about the game's own speed, so with the camera's curve and times the scope felt like the game's fixed step: its curve is stronger (a partial tilt turns clearly slower) and its turn speeds up and settles over a visible moment.
